observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with white walls, a light wood floor, a ceiling row of spotlights, and a large floor-to-ceiling mirror wall on the right. A woman with long dark hair, seen mostly from behind, wears a yellow-and-white horizontally striped short-sleeve top, a white flared mini-skirt, bright yellow leg warmers, and white sneakers. The mirror shows her front-facing reflection, so the same person appears twice: the real body in the center-left and the mirrored body on the right. The camera is fixed; background fixtures (AC unit, wall outlet, mirror seams, lights) do not shift across the frames.
visible_changes: The dancer's arms move through a sequence: initially bent with hands held low near the chest/shoulders (frames 1-7), then swinging and crossing in front of the torso and face (frames 8-13), then lifting upward with elbows bent and fists raised beside the head (frames 14-20), and finally held in that raised 'fist-up' position while the body sways and pumps (frames 21-41).

Her stance changes: legs start apart in a wide stance, then the feet draw together and stay close for the latter half, with small weight shifts and slight bouncing of the body rather than large steps.
The torso rotates subtly back and forth, and the head/hair swing accordingly during the arm motions.
The mirror reflection reproduces every one of these changes in sync, confirming it is the same person's reflection and not a second dancer.
No camera movement is detected; all apparent motion belongs to the dancer and her reflection.
outside_clip_unknowns: The start and end of the choreography (the segment is cropped mid-routine), the accompanying music or count, and any footwork or arm positions that occur before t=0 or after the last frame are not visible.
The full front view of the real dancer is never shown except through the mirror; her facial expression details outside the reflection are unseen.
uncertain_details: Whether the small vertical motions are hops or just weight shifts is ambiguous due to the low frame sampling.
Exact timing of the foot transition from wide to together stance is approximate.
